doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: Swing musicians as the stars of his generation
summary: Rowe compares swing stars to the Beatles; Fillius says the archive's guests are mostly swing-age veterans.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: That’s amazing. It’s so interesting, because I think back when I was that age, and I was a bit older, but the Beatles came in, and there was all that flak about them and that hype, and the girls loved them. And now I look at my own kids, and they have their own little stars. But the swing guys were your stars.
That was the popular music of the day.

Still are. If you note the people that we’ve brought up here to jazz concerts are primarily veterans of the swing age. That’s why they’re all in their 70s and so on and they’re not going to be around long. But fortunately you have them on tape so.
